answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with bonded stake: before joining a paid round, each agent must lock a deposit taken from its own past earnings, released only after many epochs of honest work. Minting one fake identity is cheap, but a thousand puppets means funding a thousand deposits and aging each through the slow spiral of reputation growth, while any identity proven fake is slashed to zero and its deposit burns out like a comet. In the nebula of public scrutiny where every bond is visible, mass forgery stays possible; it just stops paying.
